Rajesh Rai K. J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimants' challenging the judgment and award dated 09.02.2022 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge & MACT-V at Vijayapura in MVC No.761/2020 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal').
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7485-DB 2.

entities.text: Principal Senior Civil Judge & MACT-V at Vijayapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: We have heard the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3-insurance company and perused the materials on record.

Shantabai And Ors vs Ramappa And Ors on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75898338/
2 3.

entities.text: Shantabai And Ors vs Ramappa And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellants/claimants are the parents and brother of deceased Harish Dalawai, who died in a road traffic accident at Badagi Cross on 25.06.2020 at about 8.30 p.m.
The Tribunal was pleased to award a total compensation of Rs.16,63,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

4. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under different heads are as under:
Sl.
 Heads of compensation Amount  No.
 1. Loss of income due to Rs.15,93,000/-
 dependency  2. Towards loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
 3. Towards loss of Consortium Rs.40,000/-
 4. Towards Transportation and Rs.15,000/-
 funeral expenses

The learned counsel for the appellants fairly submitted that though the MACT awarded reasonable compensation on different heads but failed to grant compensation towards future prospects and loss of consortium in respect of appellant No.2 who is father of the deceased.
6. We have gone through the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal so also the Trial Court records.
Having perused the records, as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the appellants, the Tribunal erred by not granting compensation under the head of future prospects.

As per the judgment rendered in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, since the deceased was aged about 23 years at the time of accident, 40% of the income will have to be added towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has rightly taken the income of the deceased at Rs. 14,750/-.

Hence, if 40% of the said income is added towards furture prospect,
which is Rs. 5,900/-, the NC: 2023:KHC-K:7485-DB total income is arrived at Rs.20,650/- since the deceased was a bachelor, half of the income shall be deducted towards his personal expenses, which comes to Rs.10,325/-.
The appropriate multiplier is 18.
Thus, loss of dependency would be Rs.10,325 x 12 x 18 = Rs.22,30,200/-.
7. Deceased had three dependents, who are his mother, father and brother.
They have lost his company.

As held in the case of Pranay Sethi (referred supra) and in the case of Magma General Shantabai And Ors vs Ramappa And Ors on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75898338/
3

entities.text: Magma General Shantabai And Ors vs Ramappa And Ors on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insurance

Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, Rs.44,000/- each shall be awarded to the parents i.e. appellant No.1 and 2 towards loss of consortium i.e. a sum of Rs.88,000/-.
8.

entities.text: Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As held in the case of Pranay Sethi, Rs.16,500/- each is awarded under the head 'loss of estate'
and 'funeral expenses' i.e. a total sum of Rs.33,000/-.

As per above discussion, the claimants are NC: 2023:KHC-K:7485-DB entitled for the following amount of compensation under different heads:
1. Loss of dependency : Rs.22,30,200/-.
(10,325 x 12 x 18)
2. Loss of consortium. : Rs.88,000/-
3. Funeral expenses : Rs.16,500/-
4. Loss of estate : Rs.16,500/-
Total : Rs.23,51,200/-
Claimants
are entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.6,88,200/-.
9. For the above said discussion, we pass the following:
ORDER Appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned judgment passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge & MACT-V at Vijayapura in MVC No.761/2020 dated 09.02.2022 is modified.

The petitioners/appellants are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.23,51,200/- as against Rs.16,63,000/- awarded by the NC: 2023:KHC-K:7485-DB Tribunal and, thus are entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.6,88,200/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till payment on the enhanced amount of compensation.
Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the said amount within six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
The order passed by the Tribunal pertaining to apportionment, and deposit of the amount are kept intact.

Sd/-
